text.p: Illinois Superconductor Corp said Tuesday it named Ora Smith, currently president and chief executive officer, as chairman of the board.

He succeeds Steven Lazarus, managing general partner of ARCH Venture Partners LP, who will remain a member of the board and chairman of its executive committee. Lazarus, 66, has been chairman of the company since 1993.
Smith, 49, will become the company's first executive chairman.

Illinois Superconductor also named Edward "Ted" Laves to succeed Smith as president and chief executive officer. Laves, 50, was also elected to the six-member board of directors to replace Leonard Batterson, who has resigned.
The company said Batterson had been one of the founding venture capital investors of the company and joined the board at the beginning, in 1989.
Laves previously was executive vice president and chief operating officer.

"Ted and I will continue to work together as an effective team," Smith said in a statement. "I expect to spend an increased amount of my time developing strategic direction and relationships for the company."
The company also said Stephen Wasko, 37, chief financial officer, will assume the additional responsibilities as senior vice president of corporate development, a newly created position.
Illinois Superconductor is commercializing high temperature superconducting technology for the wireless telecommunications industry.
